source.title: On the Robustness and Generalization of Deep Learning Driven Full Waveform Inversion

record.tranche_reason: Empirically measures training–test generalization gaps and how dataset size, weight norms, and distribution drift relate to them, using a different task and measurement setup from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's reported robustness and generalization results on seismic FWI. It does not test memorization of random labels or the listed image-classification optimizer, batch-size, dropout, or sharpness claims. Cited prior work is not recorded as this study's result.
record.test_reason: The study measures seismic inverse-regression robustness and associations between generalization gaps, training-set size, weight norms and distribution drift. None tests V1–V8. Input-noise robustness and weight-norm bounds do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness. SGD, AdaGrad and AdamW are used, but their held-out performance is not separately compared.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: they claim greater robustness for MAE-trained than MSE-trained DNNs as noise increases, derive a weight-norm generalization bound, and describe synthetic FWI experiments as corroborating their theory. Their empirical norm results establish associations, with uncontrolled weight norms in the training-size experiment.
record.recipe_differences: Studies supervised seismic inverse mapping on synthetic FWI data, including noise perturbations and geological distribution drift; it does not test the claim's natural image or language classification settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise SNR and loss function change test loss and SSIM; training-set size, product of weight-matrix norms, geological fault count, and central frequency co-vary with measured generalization gap.

fits_no_version.finding: On Kimberlina CO2, MAE-trained models retain higher SSIM under noise: at SNR 0, SSIM is 0.913 versus 0.828 for MSE-trained models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training loss affects input-noise robustness in seismic inverse regression.

fits_no_version.finding: The reported gap falls from 0.045 to 0.030 as training size rises from 20k to 60k. Three architecture conditions associate larger norm products with larger gaps; weight norms are not controlled in the size experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training size and products of weight norms correlate with empirical generalization gaps in this FWI setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Every model has larger gaps with more faults and with frequencies farther from 15 Hz. Across models, the combined norm parameter generally tracks gaps, with nonmonotonic exceptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geological and source-frequency distribution shifts increase generalization gaps in these synthetic FWI experiments.

record.problems: The authors state that in the training-size experiment they could not fix the weight-norm factor, so the association is not isolated. The distribution-drift study reports varying model/parameter conditions, with the last two 1-fault results close and not monotonic. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these tables.
record.rows_left_out: None; 53 rows retained, within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error; interpolation threshold is not measured.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, local connectivity and convolution-derived initialization.
Optimizer-specific held-out comparisons and tuning-dependent differences; results are averaged across optimizers.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with gaps and comparative ranking against norm and margin measures.
Removal of examples selected by label memorization versus random removal and subsequent test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures address different claims. This does not invalidate the recorded FWI findings. Several loss-gain inconsistencies originate in Table 3 itself. No omitted result bears on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD generalization on image or language benchmarks.
Large-batch training and its generalization gap.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a correlate of generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test-accuracy change.
